description:
Mikohime Unofficial Java 28+ Configurator
A guided setup for running Starsector with modern Java 27/28

Latest release: v0.8.0

Windows x64


Recommended Java for Windows - choose Java 27 or Java 28





Experimental Linux x64


Recommended Java for Linux - choose Java 27 or Java 28





Both configurators can download and install a supported Java version automatically.

What is this?

This is an unofficial, self-contained Mikohime package with a guided configurator. It sets up Starsector to use Java 17, Java 27, or Java 28 and generates the launcher and configuration files for you.

The required Mikohime files are included with permission from the original author, Yue (Himemiko). You do not need to install the original Mikohime package separately.

Main features

Guided configuration through Configure_Me.cmd or Configure_Me.shDetects installed Java versions and can install a compatible JDK locallySupports Java 27 27+22-ea and Java 28 28+13-eaMemory and CPU recommendations based on your systemFull, Reduced, and Minimal logging modesOptional Large Pages or Linux huge-page configurationSupport for Fast RenderingOptional installation and configuration of FR Resource CacheOptional installation and configuration of OpenAL Add-onSupport for StarsectorPrepatcher 0.18.4 or newerCreates a ready-to-use platform-specific launcher

WINDOWS INSTALLATION

Windows installation
1. Download the Windows ZIP.

2. Extract everything into your Starsector installation folder.

The files should be located like this:

Starsector\starsector.exeStarsector\Configure_Me.cmdStarsector\mikohime\
3. Keep Starsector's original jre folder. Do not delete or replace it. Add a Java 27 or Java 28 JDK manually, or install either supported version from within the configurator during step 5.

4. Run Configure_Me.cmd. If Starsector is installed under Program Files or Program Files (x86), right-click the configurator and select Run as administrator.

5. Follow the prompts to select or install Java and configure memory, CPU, logging, Large Pages, Fast Rendering, FR Resource Cache, and StarsectorPrepatcher.

6. Launch the game using Miko_Rouge.bat.

If Starsector is installed under Program Files or Program Files (x86) and you enabled FR Resource Cache, run Miko_Rouge.bat as administrator for the first launch. Allow Starsector to reach the main menu so the cache directory and initial cache files can be created.

EXPERIMENTAL 64-BIT LINUX SUPPORT

Linux support is still under development. Expect bugs and compatibility issues.

Experimental Linux installation
Important: The Linux package passes build and native-library initialization checks, but it has not completed full Starsector gameplay, mod, GPU, and distribution testing. Do not treat it as a fully supported release.

1. Download the experimental Linux .tar.gz package.

2. Extract it into your Starsector installation directory beside starsector.sh.

The files should be located like this:

Starsector/starsector.shStarsector/Configure_Me.shStarsector/mikohime/
3. Open a terminal in the Starsector installation directory.

4. If necessary, make the configurator executable:

chmod +x Configure_Me.sh
5. Run the configurator:

./Configure_Me.sh
6. Follow the guided setup to select Java and configure memory, CPU, logging, huge pages, Fast Rendering, FR Resource Cache, and StarsectorPrepatcher.

7. Launch Starsector using:

./Miko_Rouge.sh
The configurator can install the supported Java builds automatically:

./Configure_Me.sh --install-java 27
./Configure_Me.sh --install-java 28
Linux requires the usual Starsector desktop runtime libraries, including X11, XRandR, XCursor, XF86VidMode, OpenAL, and ALSA.

Mods that use OpenCL, such as BoxUtil, require a working Mesa or GPU-vendor OpenCL ICD. Mikohime intentionally does not bundle libOpenCL.so because it must match your installed GPU driver.

Note: For Fast Rendering to work on Linux you need the Linux fork. https://github.com/jontyab/starsector-render

MANUAL JAVA INSTALLATION
There is an option in the configurator to download the two tested Java versions, only do this if you feel like doing the download and install manually or using a different, untested, version of Java.

Java installation information
The configurator can install Java 27 or Java 28 locally beside the Starsector launcher. It does not modify your system-wide Java installation.

For most users trying the newest Java setup, use Java 28 28+13-ea.

Example Windows locations:

Starsector\jdk-27+22\Starsector\jdk-28+13\
Example Linux locations:

Starsector/jdk-27+22/Starsector/jdk-28+13/
Keep Starsector's bundled Java runtime.

Latest Mikohime changes
v0.8.0

Added simpler Recommended, Basic, and Advanced Windows setup workflowsAdded clearer system summaries and update checks for optional componentsAdded an option to securely download, install, and enable FR Resource Cache when Fast Rendering is detectedAdded an optional Windows OpenAL Soft 1.25.1 download with backup, repair, recovery, uninstall, and audio configuration supportAdded the Toadsector launcher background for Windows and LinuxRedesigned Windows menus, navigation, recommendations, and component managementImproved the safety and consistency of configuration generationFixed Java 28 logging and compiler-directive settings across Windows workflowsFixed component download links incorrectly reporting failuresFixed menu alignment and inconsistent navigation controls
v0.7.6

Added stable 64-bit Linux support and the Miko_Rouge.sh launcherAdded Linux LWJGL, OpenAL, and JInput native librariesAdded support for the Linux Fast Rendering forkAdded separate Windows ZIP and Linux tar.gz release packagesUpdated Linux to use Starsector's native flat directory layout without starsector-coreRemoved StarsectorPrepatcher options from Linux because it is not Linux-compatible; Windows support is unchangedFixed an LWJGL native-path error that could cause a Range [0, -1) crashImproved Windows administrator, write-access, and manual Java-download handlingv0.7.5

Added an experimental 64-bit Linux configurator and generated Miko_Rouge.sh launcherAdded Linux LWJGL, OpenAL, and JInput native librariesAdded separate Windows and Linux release packagesAdded Linux Java, memory, CPU, logging, rendering, cache, and Prepatcher configurationAdded automatic Java installation on Linux with checksum validationFixed Linux support for Starsector's native flat installation layoutFixed Linux relative Java paths and launcher working-directory handlingImproved Windows manual Java-download handling

FR Resource Cache
An optional persistent resource cache for Fast Rendering

Latest release: v0.4

What does it do?

FR Resource Cache improves startup performance by allowing Fast Rendering to reuse a persistent cache instead of repeatedly reading thousands of small files from installed mod folders.

It preserves Fast Rendering's resource resolution and mod precedence. Unsupported, invalid, changed, or unavailable cache entries safely fall back to the original files.

Requirements

Fast Rendering

Mikohime J27/28+ is not required. The Mikohime configurator is only an optional, convenient way to download, install, and configure FR Resource Cache.

Manual FR Resource Cache installation
1. Download the latest FR Resource Cache release.

2. Extract fr-resource-cache-agent.jar into the appropriate location.

Windows:

Starsector\starsector-core\fr-resource-cache-agent.jar
Linux:

Starsector/fr-resource-cache-agent.jar
3. Add the FR Resource Cache Java agent before the Fast Rendering agent.

Add the following arguments to fr.vmparams. 

Windows example:

-javaagent:fr-resource-cache-agent.jar=gameRoot=.,installRoot=..,cacheDir=..\fr-resource-cache,flushDelaySeconds=30,memoryCacheMiB=128,maxFileSize=1048576
-javaagent:fr.agent.jar
Linux:

-javaagent:fr-resource-cache-agent.jar=gam
